title.en: Agencies and Awards Promoting Health, Sports and Yoga
Who supports India's athletes and honours champions?

text.en: Behind every Olympic medal and school tournament are national agencies like NCERT, CBSE, and SAI—and prestigious National Sports Awards presented every National Sports Day on 29 August.

National and state agencies promote health, sports, physical education, and yoga in India.
Educational bodies include NCERT (curriculum and textbooks), CIET (educational media), and CBSE (school sports competitions since 1988–89 and curriculum).
Sports bodies include Sports Authority of India (SAI) with 23 training centres nurturing sub-junior, junior, and senior talent, Netaji Subhas National Institute of Sports (NSNIS) Patiala, LNIPE Gwalior, and yoga institutes.
National Sports Awards are conferred annually by the Government of India on National Sports Day (29 August, Major Dhyan Chand's birth anniversary).
Key awards: Arjuna Award (instituted 1961 for outstanding athletes), Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna (formerly RGKR, highest sporting honour), Dronacharya Award (for coaches), Dhyan Chand Award (lifetime achievement), MAKA Trophy (top university), and Rashtriya Khel Protsahan Puraskar (RKPP, 2009, for corporate/organisational support).
India has dedicated educational and sports agencies to nurture young talent.
CBSE organises competitive school sports since 1988–89, while NCERT develops national curricula.
SAI runs 23 training centres across India; NSNIS Patiala and LNIPE Gwalior train elite coaches and athletes.
National Sports Awards are presented every year on 29 August—National Sports Day.
Arjuna Award (1961) honours athletes; Dronacharya Award honours coaches; MAKA Trophy honours universities.
Rashtriya Khel Protsahan Puraskar (2009) recognises organisations and corporates promoting sports.

problem.en: Match the award to its recipient: (1) Outstanding Coach, (2) Outstanding Athlete (since 1961), (3) Corporate/Entity promoting sports.

text.en: (2) Athlete -> Arjuna Award; (3) Corporate/Entity -> Rashtriya Khel Protsahan Puraskar.

why.en: Arjuna (1961) is for sportspersons and RKPP (2009) is for supporting entities.

prompt.en: Name two agencies that promote sports in India and explain three National Sports Awards.

National Sports Awards are given on 29 August (National Sports Day)
Arjuna Award honours athletes, Dronacharya honours coaches, RKPP honours organisations

commonMisconceptions.en: Confusing Dronacharya Award (for coaches) with Arjuna Award (for players)

points.en: NCERT, CIET, CBSE, SAI, NSNIS Patiala, and yoga institutes promote PE, sports, and health.
National Sports Awards are presented on 29 August (National Sports Day).
Arjuna Award (1961), Khel Ratna, Dronacharya Award, Dhyan Chand Award, MAKA Trophy, and RKPP (2009) honour excellence.
MAKA stands for Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Trophy for top-performing universities.
